title: Components of a smooth projective curve over an algebraic closure
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], and $k':=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field containing $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X_\Omega:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with projection $p:X_\Omega\to X$ [def-pc-base-change]. Then: (1) $k'$ is a finite separable field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]; put $r:=[k':k]$. (2) $X_\Omega$ is the disjoint union $X_1\amalg\cdots\amalg X_r$ of $r$ nonempty open and closed subschemes, each a proper smooth connected curve over $\Omega$ [def-sc-curves], with $\Gamma(X_j,\mathcal O_{X_j})=\Omega$. (3) For every invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], with $\mathcal L_j:=(p^*\mathcal L)|_{X_j}$ [def-pc-module-pullback], one has $r\deg_{X_j}(\mathcal L_j)=\deg_X(\mathcal L)$, with degree the Euler-characteristic difference [def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0BUG (lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections), parts (1), (3), (4), for (1); Lemma 0FD1 (lemma-baby-stein) and its proof (the factors $\kappa(s_i)\otimes_k\overline k\to\overline k$) for (2); (3) is written by an agent: $\chi$ over $k$ is $r$ times $\chi$ over $k'$ (same cohomology groups), and each $X_j=X\times_{k',\sigma_j}\Omega$ has the $\chi$ over $k'$ by flat base change (Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KH)

proof.text: Since $X$ is projective, [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes it proper; since it is a curve, [def-pc-curve] makes it a variety. Thus [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](1) makes $k'=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ a finite field extension of $k$. Smoothness gives geometric reducedness; [lem-pc-global-sections-separable] makes this extension separable. Thus $r=[k':k]\ge1$.

By [lem-pc-separable-tensor-algebraic-closure], $k'\otimes_k\Omega\cong\prod_{\sigma:k'\hookrightarrow_k\Omega}\Omega$, with $r$ factors. [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] at $i=0$ identifies this algebra with $\Gamma(X_\Omega,\mathcal O_{X_\Omega})$. Its primitive idempotents give $r$ pairwise disjoint nonempty open-and-closed subschemes $X_j$ covering $X_\Omega$; restriction gives $\Gamma(X_j,\mathcal O_{X_j})=\Omega$. Each $X_j$ is connected by [lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents]. Smoothness and properness persist under field base change by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Moreover $X$ is integral, separated and of finite type over $k'$: integrality is [def-pc-curve], while separatedness and finite type descend from the corresponding properties over $k$ along the finite extension $k'/k$; hence [def-pc-curve] applies to $X$ over $k'$. Since $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}k'$, transitivity of fibre products gives $X_\Omega=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_k\Omega)$, and the product decomposition above gives $\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_k\Omega)=\coprod_j\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ (the $j$-th factor via $\sigma_j$); hence $X_\Omega=\coprod_jX\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k',\sigma_j}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, the $j$-th piece being the locus where the $j$-th primitive idempotent is $1$, so $X_j=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k',\sigma_j}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. This identification and [lem-pc-dim-base-change] give $\dim X_j=1$. Finally, [lem-pc-clopen-smooth-proper-curve] gives smoothness and properness for each nonempty open-and-closed restriction.

proof.text: For $\mathcal F=\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal O_X$, [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] gives $H^i(X_j,\mathcal F_j)\cong H^i(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_{k',\sigma_j}\Omega$. The schemes $X$ and $X_j$ are proper over fields, and $\mathcal L$, $\mathcal O_X$ are coherent, so [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] gives finite-dimensional cohomology groups and finite alternating sums; $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because it is finite type and separated, as required by [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom]. By [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change] the dimension over $\Omega$ is $\dim_{k'}H^i(X,\mathcal F)$, while $\dim_kH^i(X,\mathcal F)=r\dim_{k'}H^i(X,\mathcal F)$. Taking finite alternating sums for both sheaves gives $\chi_k(X,\mathcal F)=r\chi_\Omega(X_j,\mathcal F_j)$, and subtraction gives $\deg_X(\mathcal L)=r\deg_{X_j}(\mathcal L_j)$ for every $j$.
